newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RACING-ROMANIA TO REBUILD RACECOURSE DESTROYED BY COMMUNISTS.
newsitem.headline: RACING-ROMANIA TO REBUILD RACECOURSE DESTROYED BY COMMUNISTS.

text.p: Bucharest's popular old racecourse, demolished in 1961 by communist authorities, is to be rebuilt under a $25 million programme, a Bucharest daily reported on Tuesday.

Evenimentul Zilei said a consortium of companies, backed by an Italian investor, had formed the "Thoroughbred Horse" group to build a track by 1999 at Mogosoaia, 16 km (10 miles) north of the capital.

It said the 58-hectare (145-acre) facility would provide for flat and harness racing and consist of turf and dirt courses with seating for up to 10,000. Some $600,000 had already been sunk into the project.

"We are looking for new investors beyond those already involved and for a measure of understanding from the new government (elected last month)," Ioan Cirje, manager of Thoroughbred Horse, told the daily.
The old Bucharest course, built in the 1930s and popular among wealthy Romanians between the two world wars, was torn down to make way for a exhibition hall.
Racing was dismissed as bourgeois under the communists, who slaughtered horses en masse after seizing power in 1948.
Two small tracks were allowed to function in Ploiesti, north of Bucharest, and in Mangalia on the Black Sea Coast, where most of the country's top animals were stabled.
